**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Escape systemd specifiers in WorkingDirectory**

When the checkout path contains a percent-based systemd specifier such as `%u` or `%h`—possible through the supported custom `--install-dir` or an existing checkout—systemd expands it instead of using the literal directory. For example, `systemd-analyze verify` on systemd 255 resolves `/tmp/foo%u` to `/tmp/fooroot`, so the service starts in the wrong or nonexistent directory and the installer eventually times out. Preserve the unquoted form required here, but escape literal `%` characters as `%%`, as this file already does for the log paths.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

`routed` is constructed with only `model` and `input`, so `delete routed.client_metadata;` is a no-op here. Either remove this line, or (if the intent is to whitelist most fields and then strip `client_metadata`) build `routed` from the incoming payload first and then delete.
`payload.client_metadata` is deleted here, but it’s deleted again later in the same function. Keeping a single deletion point reduces duplication and makes the sanitization intent clearer.

`delete payload.web_search_options;` is applied unconditionally for all forwarded chat payloads. If `web_search_options` is a supported feature for some upstreams/routes, this becomes a breaking behavior change. Consider deleting it only for providers/request profiles that reject unknown fields (or only when routing to Gemini/Kimi profiles), and document the rationale.

The sentinel value string (`\"skip_thought_signature_validator\"`) is repeated in multiple assignments. Defining it once (e.g., a module-level constant) reduces the chance of typos and makes future changes easier.

New Gemini-specific mutation of `tool_calls` is introduced here, but there’s no corresponding test in this PR validating that forwarded Gemini requests include the injected `thought_signature` fields (and that non-Gemini providers are unaffected). Add a focused test case to prevent regressions.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refresh cached names for the same session**

When Codex changes a thread title without changing the session ID, for example after an auto-generated title or a user rename, the router can return the updated `latestActiveRequest.sessionName`, but this guard only accepts a name while `activitySessionName` is nil. After the first non-empty title is cached, the Dynamic Island keeps showing that old title until a different session ID appears, so same-session renames remain stale; the session-ID equality already scopes the update, so replace the cached value when the non-empty active name differs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Good catch. You’re right, the same-session guard prevents legitimate title updates. I’ll adjust it to update the cached name when the session ID is unchanged but the non-empty title differs, while still preventing stale
  names from previous sessions.

Dropping `cmd.exe /D` re-enables Command Processor AutoRun (HKCU/HKLM) for the scheduled task, which can make the service start non-deterministic and potentially execute unexpected commands. Keep `/D` when invoking cmd.exe here.

This issue also appears on line 99 of the same file.

The `install` command swallows failures from scheduled-task creation or `/Run`, but still reports `{ installed: true }` and exits 0. This makes callers (install scripts / control plane) think the service installed successfully even when it did not, and hides the underlying error.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Map the no-thinking tier through a supported effort**

When this model is installed, Codex cannot expose this tier correctly: `src/catalog.mjs` omits `none` from every supported effort vocabulary and passes the unknown value through, which Codex silently drops from its picker; if a request nevertheless sends `none`, `ollamaCloudEffort()` in `src/api-forwarder.mjs` falls through to `high`. The advertised “No thinking” choice is therefore either unavailable or enables high reasoning instead. Represent it with a Codex-supported rung and explicitly translate that rung to Ollama's `none`, with a routing test covering the translation.

The headerless-SSE sniff in `EmptyCompletionGuard` and the one in `prepareEventStreamRetry` disagree on what counts as SSE. `prepareEventStreamRetry` uses `HEADERLESS_SSE_PREFIX` (router.mjs:394), which explicitly tolerates a UTF-8 BOM, leading comment lines (`: ...`), and leading blank lines. The guard's `SSE_FIELD_LINE` (empty-completion-guard.mjs:4) requires the buffer to start with `event:`/`data:`/`id:`/`retry:` immediately — no BOM, no leading comment, no blank line.

Concrete failure: an upstream whose first bytes are `: keepalive\n\n` (some gateways emit an initial comment) is classified as `#eventStream = false` by the guard during the first attempt, so the whole stream is passed through untouched and the empty-completion gate never runs. The same bytes on the retry path are accepted by `prepareEventStreamRetry` and piped with `pipelineContentType = "text/event-stream"`. So the first attempt silently skips the guard while the retry detects it — inconsistent, and the empty-completion detection is exactly the thing that must not silently skip.

Suggestion: extract a single shared prefix predicate (tolerating BOM + leading comment/blank lines, i.e. the `HEADERLESS_SSE_PREFIX` behavior) and use it in both places, so a stream is classified identically on both attempts.

The 30s / 1 MiB release path silently disables the empty-completion gate for long-thinking turns. When `#release()` fires (byte cap at line 189, timer at line 271), the stream is relayed as-is and `#empty` is never set — `isEmpty()` stays false. That is the right conservative choice for "we can't hold a real turn hostage", but it means the exact failure this PR is fixing (reasoning-only turn that completes with no output) still slips through silently when the reasoning phase takes longer than 30s or exceeds 1 MiB. The hold-budget guards exist to avoid unbounded buffering, not to make the failure mode conditional on duration.

Suggestion: instead of dropping the verdict entirely on budget exhaustion, mark the guard as "indeterminate" and have `handleResponses` record a distinguishable usage-event marker (e.g. `emptyCompletionGuardReleased: true`) on that turn. The operator keeps the telemetry that says "this turn may have been an empty completion we chose not to retry", and the retry behaviour stays as-is. Without a marker, a 40-second empty completion looks identical to a healthy 40-second turn in `usage-events.jsonl`.

Non-SSE data blocks are classified as "no content" and can turn a healthy turn into a retried one. In `#contentOf`, a block whose `data:` payload is not parseable JSON (or whose event type is unknown) falls through to `return false`. For a gateway that mixes a non-JSON sentinel line (e.g. an `: keepalive` comment is fine since it has no `data:`, but a `data: pong` from a custom heartbeat) with the real SSE events, the guard would hold the stream and, once `response.completed` arrives, mark the whole turn empty — even though a genuine `output_text.delta` earlier in the stream was already classified as content and `#sawContent` is true.

Wait — checking `#classifyBlock` again: content detection happens first, and `#release()` fires as soon as any content event is seen, so a genuine delta releases the stream before a later non-JSON block can matter. The risk is narrower: only streams where the *first* meaningful event is the terminal one (a "whole turn rides on `response.completed`" gateway) and the completed payload itself fails JSON.parse. For those, the turn is treated as empty and retried even though it carried output.

Suggestion: when the terminal event's data fails to parse, prefer releasing the stream (indeterminate) over declaring it empty — a parse failure at the terminal event is not evidence of "nothing was produced".

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip the venv probe for a custom LiteLLM launcher**

When `MODEL_ROUTER_LITELLM_BIN` supplies a custom launcher, the bundled `.venv` may intentionally be absent, but this unconditional probe aborts before the selected launcher is started. This breaks the existing `startup-cleanup.test.mjs`, and the fresh-checkout CI jobs run `npm test` after only `npm ci`, so they have no `.venv`; running that test now exits here with `spawnSync .../.venv/bin/python ENOENT` instead of exercising startup cleanup. Gate the probe on use of the bundled LiteLLM launcher or ensure the selected custom runtime is probed instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Actually recreate venvs rejected for a missing home**

When `pyvenv.cfg` names a missing home but the copied `.venv/bin/python` or Windows `python.exe` still exists, this correctly makes the step run, but both uv installer branches only call `uv venv` when that launcher is absent (`bin/install` lines 104-106 and `install.ps1` lines 250-253). They consequently run `uv pip install` against the damaged environment without rewriting `pyvenv.cfg`, which can either fail or leave every subsequent update detecting the same corruption rather than rebuilding it; the unusable-home result must cause the installer to clear/recreate the venv.

`integerToken()` only rewrites tokens that round-trip through JS `Number` as a safe integer. That means values like `9007199254740993.0` (still a valid u64) will remain `... .0` and continue to be rejected by Codex as a floating-point number. You can safely drop a trailing `.0+` fraction lexically (no precision loss) even when the magnitude exceeds `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.

`tracked.txt` appears to be a leftover test artifact. It’s already created/modified inside `test/installer-scripts.test.mjs` using a temporary checkout, so committing it in the repository root is unnecessary and may confuse future diffs or tooling. Consider removing this file from the PR unless it’s intentionally part of the product.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse integrality from the token before coercing**

When a tool supplies a very small or high-precision fractional argument, converting the token to a binary `Number` can round it to a safe integer, so valid inputs such as `1e-324` and `9007199254740991.4` are silently rewritten to `0` and `9007199254740991`. Conversely, a valid whole u64 such as `9007199254740992.0` is left as a float and remains rejected by Codex because it is outside JavaScript's safe-integer range. Determine whether the decimal/exponent token is mathematically integral without first rounding it through `Number`, then separately enforce the destination integer range.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Fixed in `0f9bfa8`. Integrality is decided from the token spelling now, so `9007199254740993.0` becomes `9007199254740993` without going through `Number`.

Fixed in `0f9bfa8`. The rewriter no longer asks JS `Number` whether a token is integral, so `1e-324` and `9007199254740991.4` stay as written. Tests cover both cases.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle comments on managed provider headers**

When the managed provider header has a valid trailing TOML comment, such as `[model_providers.codex-router] # router`, this exact comparison classifies the router-owned table as foreign. `clean()` consequently hoists the old table, and `enabledContents()` appends another canonical table with the same name, leaving duplicate TOML tables that prevent Codex from loading the configuration. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve Node's configured proxy dispatcher**

Replacing that dispatcher unconditionally with a bare `Agent` bypasses the configured proxy, so every native and routed upstream fetch fails on networks that require it. Preserve or wrap the existing proxy dispatcher while disabling HTTP/2 rather than overwriting it.

In streaming mode with `mayRetry`, `holding` can still be true when the upstream finishes (e.g., short output/no tools, or a progress-only stop before retry). In that case `emitPendingDeltas()` returns early and the buffered deltas are never flushed; the response can end up sending only the role chunk + final finish chunk with no content/tool_call deltas.

Before finalizing the stream, force-release any hold and flush pending deltas so the client always receives the buffered output.

`mergeMappedUsage()` returns `first`/`second` unchanged when either side is missing. In the retry path this can drop the `retries` marker (and any merge intent) if one attempt lacks a `response.completed` usage block, despite the forwarder having performed a retry.

Since this helper is only called when a retry occurred, make the early-return cases still set `retries: 1` on whichever usage object exists.

`tracked.txt` appears unrelated to the Grok OAuth retry changes and overlaps with a filename used in `test/installer-scripts.test.mjs` as a temporary git fixture. If this file was added accidentally, it should be removed from the PR to avoid introducing a stray top-level tracked file.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip progress retry when tool_choice is none**

When an OpenAI-compatible caller sends function `tools` but explicitly sets `tool_choice: "none"`, this still enables the progress-only retry. `toResponsesRequest()` preserves that `tool_choice`, so the retry cannot produce the tool call required by `shouldPreferRetryTurn()` and we only add a second billed request plus latency before returning the first answer. Gate `mayRetry` on tool calls being allowed, not just on tool definitions being present.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the first answer when the retry stream aborts**

If the first attempt is a completed progress-only stop but the retry receives a 200 response whose SSE body then terminates or errors while being read, this `await` rejects and the outer handler returns a generic forwarder error before any response was sent. That discards the valid first answer even though the retry was only supposed to improve it when it produced a tool call; catch read failures on the second stream and fall back to the first turn as the non-OK retry path does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark failed progress retries in usage**

When the retry request gets a non-OK response or no body, this branch logs the failure but then falls through with the original `turn.usage` and leaves `retried` false, so the client/router usage observer records an ordinary successful 200 even though the turn waited on a second upstream attempt. Add a retry marker without inventing token counts so usage-events and provider stats can distinguish this rescued turn from one that never retried.

**[bug]** Default icon style is `.provider` (`menuBarIconStyle = .provider` when the key is absent), but `MenuBarIconView.assetName` only maps openai/grok/kimi/deepseek/anthropic/commandcode/github-copilot/chutes. The same target already has a complete, documented `ProviderIcon` in `IslandOverlay.swift` (opencode*, kilo-free, zai-*, qwen-plan, ollama-cloud/local, clinepass, minimax-token-plan, meta) and `ModelRouterTrayApp.swift` already uses it for quota rows. `assetExtension` is also keyed off `providerID` instead of the resolved asset name, so even a later prefix map would pick `.png` for `opencode-go` / `kilo-free`. Consequence: after upgrade, GLM/Qwen/Ollama/OpenCode/Cline/MiniMax/Meta/Kilo/local users lose the old activity dot and get a 6pt circle; while `activityState != .idle`, `StatusItemLabel` then adds a second 5pt badge (`menuBarIconStyle != .indicator`), so the menu bar shows two dots.

**Suggestion:** Delete the duplicate loader and render `ProviderIcon(providerID:size:)` for `.provider`. If a fallback is still needed, use the same `cpu` symbol `ProviderIcon` already uses, and only show the side badge when the main view is not already a status circle.

**[bug]** Standard mode still renders usage or concurrent-provider text after the model-name toggle, but reserved width is now applied only when `menuBarShowModelName` is true (`.frame(width: nil)` otherwise). The previous `reservedWidth = 180` existed specifically to keep the `NSStatusItem` anchor stable while that text changed. Hiding the name therefore makes the status item jump between `"45% left"`, localized remaining strings, and `"Grok + Claude"` as activity starts and stops.

**Suggestion:** Keep a stable reserved width whenever standard mode still shows trailing usage/activity text (or reserve a smaller but fixed width for the usage-only layout). Do not make the status-item width follow the live string.

**[bug]** Icon-only mode uses `.frame(minWidth: 18)` with no max/fixed width. Idle is a 14pt icon; non-idle non-indicator styles add a 5pt badge and 4pt spacing (~23pt), and the icon also `scaleEffect`s to 1.4 during `attentionPulse`. The design asked for a compact reserved slot (~22–26pt / ~24pt), not a growing `minWidth`. The item will shift its neighbors when activity starts, and the pulse can overflow the 18pt slot.

**Suggestion:** Give icon-only a fixed compact width (around 24pt) that already includes the badge, and pulse inside that frame instead of changing the status-item’s measured size.

**[suggestion]** `chooseCustomIconImage()` persists `url.path` only. The bundle is ad-hoc signed and not sandboxed, so a still-present user-readable file will usually reload after restart, but a moved, renamed, iCloud-evicted, or deleted file fails silently: `customImage` returns nil and the menu bar falls back to `cpu` while Settings still shows `URL.lastPathComponent`. `customImage` also calls `NSImage(contentsOfFile:)` from a SwiftUI computed property, so every `RouterStore` publish (activity poll can fire every 1s) re-reads the file.

**Suggestion:** Copy the chosen image into Application Support (or keep a security-scoped bookmark plus a cached `NSImage` on `RouterStore`). If the file is gone, clear or flag the setting and show that in the custom-image row instead of the stale filename.

**[suggestion]** Absent `ModelRouterTray.menuBarIconStyle` becomes `.provider`. Every existing install therefore upgrades from the pulsing activity dot to a provider mark without opting in. Issue #307 asked to keep the current layout available; the design’s “preserve default mode” language describes the old Icon/Dot + name + usage row. Combined with the incomplete map in Issue 1, this is a silent visual change for everyone and a functional regression for unmapped providers.

**Suggestion:** Default missing keys to `.indicator` so current installs keep the shipped look. Use `.provider` only after an explicit Settings choice (or a one-time migration if you truly want the new default for fresh installs only).

**[suggestion]** New defaults load/defaulting lives only in `RouterStore.init` / the five setters. There is no extracted pure resolver and no Swift test, unlike `resolveIslandMode` + `IslandModeTests`. The PR’s “43 passed” run is `test/tray-install.test.mjs`, `tray-rebuild.test.mjs`, and `tray-service-windows.test.mjs`; those suites do not instantiate `RouterStore` or render `StatusItemLabel`. `LocalizationTests` only checks table-key parity, which these new strings already satisfy.

**Suggestion:** Extract a `resolveMenuBarSettings(...)` helper (unknown raw values, missing keys, default icon style) and add Swift tests in `apps/macos/ModelRouterTray/Tests`, the same way island mode is tested.

**[suggestion]** The new `.help(tooltipText)` string is hardcoded English (`"Codex Router · \(provider) (\(state)) · \(usage)"`). Settings labels were translated in all five tables, so icon-only mode — the case that most needs the tooltip — is the one that stays English.
